messages:
maria.conley: heads up — after the RBAC change this morning the DSAR delete worker ran but we couldn't produce deletion proof for a handful of EU subjects. audit log shows the job ran but no 'delete-confirm' entries were written. cc @diane-privacy

ajay: hmm. did the worker throw permission errors or KMS decrypt failures? can you paste the short log lines?

maria.conley: logs look like this:```2026-02-10T09:12:34Z delete-worker[eid=xy123] INFO start delete job user=eu-123
2026-02-10T09:12:34Z delete-worker[eid=xy123] ERROR persist-proof access_denied: iam.roles.storage.writer required
2026-02-10T09:12:35Z delete-worker[eid=xy123] WARN kms: decrypt failed: key not found```

kevin-sre: OK two things jump out: 1) the worker lost storage write role (RBAC change) and 2) a KMS key lookup failed. they can both block proof generation.

adja (typo fix) — @ajay can you confirm whether the KMS key got rotated or rekeyed during the maintenance window?

ajay: looking now — I see a key rotation event at 2026-02-10T09:05:00Z for projects/redwood-prod/keys/dsar-proofs. rotation created new key version but IAM binding for service-account:delete-worker@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com was not propagated to the new version (weird). that would explain decrypt errors.

diane-privacy: legal needs an unbroken chain for erasure proof. if we can't produce the original confirmation entry, we have to document the gap and create a retention-exception/forensics ticket. can ops confirm whether any customer-facing deletes were impacted?

kevin-sre: quick mitigations: 1) re-add storage.writer role to delete-worker SA (rollback of RBAC tweak) 2) add cryptoKeyVersion IAM bindings to new key version OR set key to allow service account decryption 3) rerun the delete-proof job for affected batch ids. I can run 1+2 now if approved.

maria.conley: please go ahead, kevin. I already opened a backup of the proof bucket snapshot (s3://priv-proofs/snap-20260210-0910) before we started touching permissions.

ops-bot: deploy-notify: RBAC-change rollback started by kevin-sre at 2026-02-10T09:30:12Z.

ajay: after binding fix I ran a local decrypt test: ```gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=prod --key=dsar-proofs --ciphertext-file=ct.bin --plaintext-file=pt.bin --impersonate-service-account=service-account:delete-worker@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com``` returns success.

kevin-sre: rollback and key binding update complete. requeued the affected job ids: [eu-123, eu-124, eu-125]. starting replay now.

maria.conley: replay finished for those ids. proof entries created for eu-123 and eu-124; eu-125 failed due to a stale snapshot (object not found) — looks like a retention window mismatch.

diane-privacy: for eu-125 we need to escalate: evidence that we attempted deletion, note missing payload due to snapshot expiry, and file a retention-exception for that subject. @legal-bot please flag with required fields: subject id, attempt timestamps, proof logs, snapshot id.

legal-bot: retention-exception request template: please include subject identifier, deletion-attempt timestamps, affected object keys, storage lifecycle policy version, and mitigation plan. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/RetentionExceptions. I will route to DataPrivacy.

kevin-sre: created ticket RE-2026-045 with logs and snapshot metadata. attaching: /var/log/delete-worker/2026-02-10/xy123.log and s3://priv-proofs/snap-20260210-0910/manifest.json

maria.conley: thanks. follow-up action items: (1) add a preflight check to the DSAR pipeline to validate KMS binding and SA roles before job start, (2) alert on delete-proof gaps to eng-security, (3) legal to confirm retention-exception acceptance. I'll write a short postmortem.

diane-privacy: approving preflight approach. legal will review RE-2026-045 and reply with next steps within 48h.

kevin-sre: quick note for ops: patch scheduled to ensure new KMS key versions inherit SA bindings automatically. I'll add that to the ksm rotation runbook.

maria.conley: all good. closing thread once legal confirms. :thumbsup:
